International scholarships International Undergraduate Scholarship Starting an undergraduate degree at ARU? This scholarship can help with the costs of study. The scholarship is a fee discount. We will deduct it from your tuition fees in each year of your course. Value There are two levels of award. Lower award – up to £5,000 £2,000 in the first year of your course* £1,000 in each subsequent year of your course (up to a maximum of three subsequent years) You must successfully complete each year to get £1,000 in the subsequent year *If you are studying at ARU in Writtle, you will automatically get £2,000 in your first year. Higher award – up to £7,000 £4,000 in the first year of your course £1,000 in each subsequent year of your course (up to a maximum of three subsequent years) You must successfully complete each year to get £1,000 in the subsequent year Eligibility You should be: an international student (international tuition fee payer) a new student, joining ARU for the first time starting a taught undergraduate course at ARU in Cambridge, Chelmsford, Peterborough or Writtle studying full-time, unless there are exceptional circumstances preventing full-time study starting in Year 1 to receive £2,000 (Lower Award) or £4,000 (Higher Award) If you are starting in Year 2 or Year 3, you will receive £1,000 in each year of your course. If you have Accredited Prior Certified Learning (APCL), discounts will be adjusted on a pro-rata basis. This scholarship cannot be combined with any other scholarships. However, you can get a Full Payment Discount in Year 1 if you pay your fees in full before teaching starts. The scholarship is not available during work placements or for: pre-sessional English courses ARU College courses foundation degrees online / distance learning courses degree apprenticeships or other work-based degrees Study Abroad programmes Depending on the terms and conditions of your funding body, you may not be eligible if you are: sponsored by an organisation such as an employer, charitable body, or government department receiving federal tuition fee loans How to apply There is no need to apply. You will automatically receive our International Undergraduate Scholarship if you meet the eligibility criteria. You must meet all conditions of registration before the scholarship is awarded. If you withdraw from your course, we will adjust the scholarship on a pro-rata basis. How we assess your application We review applications from all eligible international students. For the Lower Award, we assess the overall standard of your application, including entry qualifications. For the Higher Award, we assess the overall standard of your application. It should exceed minimum requirements, including entry qualifications. Questions? Speak to our international team. Email [email protected] or call+44 1245 683680. How to apply Step 4 - Receive our decision on your application We aim to provide an initial response and/or a decision on your application as soon as possible. Provided you meet our English, academic and immigration requirements, you'll be likely to receive an offer from us. Accepting your offer If you applied to us directly, you need to accept your offer on your Applicant Portal within 28 days (or sooner depending on when you applied). You will receive instructions on how to access your Portal in your offer letter. If you applied to us through UCAS, you will need to accept your offer through UCAS Hub . You will need your UCAS Personal ID and password to log in, which UCAS will have provided to you when you applied. Deadlines apply so please refer to the UCAS website to check for the deadline to accept your offer. Meeting your conditions To meet the requirements of a conditional offer, you’ll need to provide copies of all documents requested (for example, academic qualifications and English language test results. You can upload all your required documents to your Applicant Portal. Sometimes, we may come back to you and ask for additional supporting documents. This will be communicated to you via your Applicant Portal and by email. Therefore, it's very important that the contact details on your application form are correct and up to date and that you check your email regularly for correspondence from us. Paying your deposit Aside from any academic conditions, you will also be asked to pay a deposit. Please note that all full fee paying international students will be required to pay a deposit before being issued with a CAS . Currently, the deposit for Undergraduate and Postgraduate taught courses is £4,000; further details will be included in your offer letter. Refunds of any deposit paid will be administered in accordance with the Rules, Regulations and Procedures for Students, which you will receive with your offer letter. A refund of a deposit may not be given in the event of a refusal of a visa arising from giving false or incomplete information to the United Kingdom Visas and Immigration (UKVI). To pay your deposit, as well as your fees, visit our fee payments page . Issuing your CAS Before we issue a CAS, you'll need to complete our Immigration History Form. You may also be asked to provide us with the documents you are going to use for your visa application. For more information about obtaining a CAS, please visit our immigration page . Once you receive your CAS, you'll be able to apply for your visa, although keep in mind that it will be issued no earlier than three months before the start date of your course . I haven't heard from you yet... Check your email, including the junk folder. We may have requested further information or additional documents from you. Contact your country representative or agent (if applicable). If you're a direct applicant and you haven’t heard from us in ten business days, please email [email protected] . Scholarships and bursaries Alumni Scholarship If you’ve already completed a degree at ARU and want to study a postgraduate course, this scholarship is for you. The Alumni Scholarship is a fee discount. We’ll deduct it from your tuition fees. Value There are two scholarships available: 20% off your fees if you achieved a 2:2 or above, and are applying for a postgraduate taught degree or a £400 discount if you're applying for a postgraduate research degree Duration The scholarship is awarded in the first year of the postgraduate taught or research degree (full-time) or across both years (part-time). Eligibility You should have completed one of the following: Full honours degree (BA/BSc, BEng, BOptom) Full Masters degree (MA/MSc, MEng) Postgraduate Certificate (PG Cert) Postgraduate Diploma (PG Dip) You must be: an ARU alumnus starting a new postgraduate taught or research award (in the first semester of study), either full-time or part-time starting your course in the 2026-27 academic year from the UK or an EU/EEA student who remains eligible for student finance . International students should see our International Alumni Scholarship . There's no time limit on when you completed your ARU award. Your award can be from predecessor institutions, or an ARU-validated degree at one of our partner institutions . This scholarship is not available for: degree apprenticeship or distance learning courses applicants who are receiving fee discounts from external agencies such as HEE, GMC or NMC MA Social Work students who receive the fee contribution from NHS Social Work Bursaries. How to apply There's no need to apply. You'll automatically be assessed for our Alumni Scholarship as part of your application. We’ll let you know if you’re eligible when we send you a conditional offer. rules.future_year_note: ARU publishes £1,000 in subsequent years, for up to three subsequent years, subject to successful completion. Those future-year rules are not imported by this command.
rules.source_period_note: Current published policy does not name an academic year. Saved against the reviewed 2027/28 course cohort; recheck before enrolment.
